industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the counter-case the strongest it has been and named: the US ten-year is 4.83% (down 50 basis points in two months; Goldman Sachs, 20 to 26-Nov), 33 basis points from the sector rows' trigger (back to D under 4.5%), Oppenheimer's 2027 theme is 'beneficiaries of lower bond yields' and Bell (20-Nov) likes UK real estate and homebuilders; the table's Underweights led the week's rebound. Held at F because the yield fell as a safety bid inside a tightening of financial conditions (Mark Wilson: 100 to 150 basis points), European yields rose this week with ECB minutes leaning to hikes, and every property sector reads D or F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26). This is the first row I would lift if the ten-year goes through 4.5% on an easing read. No Pool name, no live holding.

sector.key: N.4. Real estate - logistics and industrial
sector.why: Double Underweight, carried: the longest-duration, lowest-yield end of property, where the multiple has furthest to fall as real yields rise; the ten-year 4.83%, 33 basis points from the trigger. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior). No Pool name. Counter-case: re-shoring demand is real and this is its property; back to D if the US ten-year falls under 4.5% on an easing read.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Belgium this week; one live holding, D'Ieteren (2.66%); Pool names Azelis, UCB, Ageas, CMB.TECH. Moves to D if a second source names Belgium or a spread reading is read widening.
